articles.headline: Sources: Grizzlies waiving former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr.
articles.description: The Grizzlies are waiving 2025 No. 18 pick Walton Clayton Jr. and Micah Peavy ahead of Monday's roster cut-down deadline.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると：グリズリーズ、元1巡目指名のウォルター・クレイトン・Jr.をウェイバー指定
articles.descriptionJa: グリズリーズは月曜日のロスター削減期限を前に、2025年ドラフト18位指名のウォルトン・クレイトン・Jr.とマイカ・ピービーをウェイバー指定する。
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies are waiving 2025 No. 18 pick Walter Clayton Jr. and former second-round pick Micah Peavy, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

The moves helped Memphis finalize its roster for the regular season by the 5 p.m. ET cut-down deadline.

The Grizzlies entered Monday with 17 players on standard contracts and three more on two-way deals. Sixteen of the 17 contracts are guaranteed. Jaylen Wells' $2.3 million salary became guaranteed Monday.

Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr., Jock Landale, John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range.

Peavy, the 40th pick of the 2025 draft, played 61 games as a rookie with the New Orleans Pelicans last season, including four starts. He averaged 4.3 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.0 assists.

articles.headline: Stephen Jones says Brian Schottenheimer has full support of Cowboys' ownership
articles.description: Brian Schottenheimer has the full support of Cowboys ownership, Stephen Jones said Monday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: スティーブン・ジョーンズ、ブライアン・ショットハイマーはカウボーイズのオーナー陣から全面的な支持を得ていると語る
articles.descriptionJa: スティーブン・ジョーンズは月曜日、ダラスの「105.3 The Fan」にて、ブライアン・ショットハイマーはカウボーイズのオーナー陣から全面的な支持を得ていると語った。
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Twenty-three games into his tenure as the Dallas Cowboys head coach, Brian Schottenheimer has a 9-13-1 record and the full support of ownership.

"Absolutely. There's not any question in Jerry's and I's mind," executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. "We feel really good ... about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."

The Cowboys are 2-4 after Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, dropping two straight games. Next week they play the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles on ESPN's "Monday Night Football," looking to avoid the second three-game losing streak in Schottenheimer's tenure.

Schottenheimer said he did not need the public show of support.

"I think at the end of the day, I'm focused on the process of turning this around for myself, the players," Schottenheimer said Monday. "Certainly not good enough. We're disappointed with where we're at. We know we need to play better. We know we can play better. And I think at the end of the day, we've got the right guys to do that."

The Cowboys have struggled defensively for the entire season, but the offense, where Schottenheimer serves as the playcaller, has been off the last two games. Dak Prescott has been intercepted four times. Their 29 points in the last two games is the fewest in a two-game span of starts made by Prescott since Weeks 5-6 of the 2024 season.

The Cowboys' running game is 30th in the NFL with 456 yards through six games. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were also kept in check by the Packers as Prescott averaged 4.8 yards per attempt.

"In terms of changes, no, we're going to get back to work and we'll figure it out," Schottenheimer said. "We have great trust in our offense. I'm not concerned about our offense. Again, last two weeks, the last two weeks. We own that. It is what it is. It's not been good enough, but we also have a history of being really explosive, really good. And we've done that not only last year, but in four of our games this year."

Asked if he would want his team to be angry or measured following the last two games, Schottenheimer said, "I always like guys that are angry."

"I'd say right now I'm pretty pissed off," he said, adding, "I think they're pissed off too."

Four of the Cowboys' next five opponents -- Philadelphia, Arizona, Indianapolis and Tennessee -- are a combined 7-17. On Nov. 15 they host the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers.

"We're ready for a win," Schottenheimer said.

It's not quite do or die, but it's not far off.

"I'll never not take accountability for the fact that we're 2-4," Schottenheimer said. "It's not what we planned on being. That's not where the standard of what we're trying to do is. articles.headline: Maddison scores in 'dream' return as Spurs get 1st EPL win of season
articles.description: An emotional James Maddison said it was like a "dream" to produce a goal and help Tottenham climb off the bottom of the Premier League with a 3-1 home win.
articles.headlineJa: マディソンが「夢のような」復帰戦でゴール、スパーズが今季EPL初勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 感極まったジェームズ・マディソンは、ゴールを決めてトッテナムの3-1でのホーム勝利に貢献し、プレミアリーグの最下位脱出を助けられたことは「夢のよう」だったと語った。
articles.body:
An emotional James Maddison said it was like a "dream" to produce a goal and help Tottenham climb off the bottom of the Premier League with a 3-1 home win -- their first of the season in the league -- over Coventry City on Monday.

Maddison marked his first start in 526 days after back-to-back knee injuries with a special strike in the 14th minute after he sent a first-time effort over Carl Rushworth before he marked it with a trademark darts celebration.

Spurs playmaker Maddison was the best player on the pitch during an even first half but Coventry levelled through Jack Rudoni only four minutes into the second period, sparking a frantic period.

Boss Roberto De Zerbi watched Omar Marmoush fire Tottenham back in front with 58 minutes played before Tosin Adarabioyo, Andy Robertson and Marmoush were forced off with issues, allowing Dejan Kulusevski to make his own comeback after 17 months of injury hell.

Kulusevski received a special ovation and minutes later Ben Davies ensured the Swedish attacker would celebrate his comeback with all three points when Davies' scuffed effort beat Rushworth to earn Spurs an overdue first league victory of the campaign.

Maddison, who only returned from anterior cruciate ligament damage last April, said after impressing against his hometown club: "I hoped [to start].

"I spoke to the gaffer about it this week and just feeling like the right moment for me to go back into the starting XI after a stop-start start to the season.

"I just wanted to play well, show my quality and show what the team's missed in the last 18 months, or whatever it is since my last start.

"The gaffer asked me to play and said he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side so hopefully I did that. And obviously a goal like that is always nice."

It was Maddison's first goal since his last start -- a 3-1 victory over Bodo/Glimt in the semifinals of the Europa League at the end of the 2024-25 season.

"They're the ones you dream of. Without going too deep into it, them dark days last year, recovering from the ACL, you dream of them moments, them goals and that is the light at the end of the tunnel," Maddison told Sky Sports.

"That is why I was a bit emotional and I felt really proud of Dejan Kulusevski as well because him coming back.

"I knew exactly that feeling of him stepping onto the pitch after that time out, but those moments and goals make it all worth it."

articles.headline: 49ers WR Mike Evans reps Bay Area with Curry jersey, leads NFL Week 6's arrivals
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: 49ersのWRマイク・エバンス、カリーのジャージでベイエリアを象徴、NFL第6週の入場をリード
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日の入場を毎週のファッションショーへと変え続けている。
articles.body:
Fall fashion is finding its footing as the NFL enters Week 6.

With October in full swing, players are navigating a mix of crisp  temperatures and lingering warmth as they make their pregame arrivals.

The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos kicked off the week Thursday night with temperatures around 50 degrees in Denver, setting the stage for layered looks. Sunday's slate offered a similar fall feel in Cleveland, Foxborough and Philadelphia, where temperatures are expected to hover in the 50s. Meanwhile, warmer conditions in Tampa Bay and Los Angeles gave players more room to experiment with lighter ensembles.

From all black leather fits like Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to fur coats like Houston Texans QB C.J. Stroud wore in London, here are Week 6's most fashionable fits that caught our eye:

Primetime arrivals

Bay Area basketball pride met bold fall style ahead of the San Francisco 49ers' "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Washington Commanders. Wide receiver Mike Evans paid homage to Stephen Curry in a black Golden State Warriors No. 30 jersey, paired with black cargo pants and sneakers. Defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa took a dressier approach, layering a fuzzy green-and-white cardigan over a white shirt and black tie. Brown corduroy pants, a black beret and amber-tinted glasses rounded out his look.

Ahead of "Sunday Night Football" against the Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin leaned into fall style with a burgundy leather jacket and matching pants over a black shirt. He accessorized with tinted shades, patterned shoes and an oversized "Z" pendant.

 Sunday's best

No player quantifies pound-for-pound among the best in the game quite like the 170-pound Philadelphia Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith on the field and with his gameday tunnel fit.
 
This week, Smith returned from injury to the Eagles lineup with a European style look blending a clean stone mélange Bottega Veneta wool jacket with a classic but fly dress shirt, tie and tailored trousers. Smith's shiny Black tabi loafer work well with this combo.
 
And don't forget about the accessories -- Smith's Louis Vuitton Porte-Documents Voyage PM briefcase and Saint Laurent sunglasses complete the fit.
 
The extremely competitive A.J. Brown once said "nobody in this league is touching Smitty when it comes to dressing with suits" referencing the unique, sleek custom pieces that Smith wears often courtesy his primary bespoke haberdasher Brian Alexander.
 
But fashion means versatility, and this look from Smith shows his range.

articles.headline: Rams suffer several major injuries, including to WR Adams, who's out 6-10 weeks
articles.description: Rams wideout Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and he will be sidelined for six to 10 weeks, coach Sean McVay announced.
articles.headlineJa: ラムスに主力級の負傷者が続出、WRアダムスは6〜10週間の離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ラムスのワイドレシーバー、ダバンテ・アダムスが日曜日のカーディナルズ戦での敗北中にハムストリングを断裂。ショーン・マクベイ監督の発表によると、6〜10週間の戦線離脱となる。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams wide receiver Davante Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, head coach Sean McVay said Monday.

Adams' injury, which McVay called a ruptured semitendinosus, appeared to happen late in the fourth quarter of the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals while he was running a route into the end zone.

Adams will undergo a procedure to repair his ruptured hamstring, which will be performed by Dr. Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Adams hopes to return on the front end of the six- to 10-week time frame, as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible, the source said.

In his Monday news conference, McVay gave a long list of injury updates. In addition to Adams, McVay said nose tackle Poona Ford will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps and defensive tackle Kobie Turner will miss "a handful of weeks" with a groin injury. McVay said the Rams will likely put Turner on injured reserve, which would sideline him for at least four games.

McVay also said kicker Blake Grupe, whom the Rams placed on injured reserve on Monday, tore an ACL. The Rams have not yet made a corresponding move at kicker, but McVay said the team is "working on some different options." The Rams will be working out veteran kickers Brandon McManus and Matt Prater on Tuesday, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

Pass rusher Myles Garrett, who had knee surgery in mid-September, will not return to practice this week, McVay said. Garrett has missed the past five games.

McVay said cornerback Trent McDuffie, who did not play Sunday after injuring his groin last week in practice, is "progressing."

"He's feeling much better," McVay said. "The hope is progress this week and kind of determine his status at the end of this week."

In six games this season, Adams, a six-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro, has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns.

McVay said the Rams will talk about whether they will add a receiver to the roster with Adams missing an extended period of time. Along with Puka Nacua and Adams, the Rams have wide receivers Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman on their roster.

The Rams entered the season as 5-1 favorites at DraftKings to win the Super Bowl, according to ESPN Research. Those odds fell to 10-1 after Sunday's loss to the Cardinals and are now 12-1.

articles.headline: Hornets, Brandon Miller agree to 5-year, $209M rookie extension
articles.description: The Hornets and forward Brandon Miller agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension.
articles.headlineJa: ホーネッツ、ブランドン・ミラーと5年総額2億900万ドルのルーキー延長契約で合意
articles.descriptionJa: ホーネッツとフォワードのブランドン・ミラーは、5年総額2億900万ドルのルーキー規模の契約延長に合意した。
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller has agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension, representatives AJ Vaynerchuk and Joey Middleton of VaynerSports told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. 

Miller, who turns 24 next month, had a career season in 2025-26, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 38.3% shooting from 3 in 65 regular-season games. He was also able to stay mostly healthy following a season in which he appeared in just 27 games.

 

Miller, along with then-rookie Kon Knueppel, helped spearhead a surprise run to the postseason in the second half of last year, where they fell in the second play-in game. He was especially key to Charlotte's midseason turnaround, as the Hornets went 41-24 with Miller available and 3-14 without him. He missed a chunk of the beginning of the season due to a shoulder injury. 

Miller underwent surgery in May to address the stability of that shoulder, but he has since fully recovered and appeared in preseason for Charlotte.

Heading into his fourth year in the league, Miller will be stepping into an even bigger role for the Hornets this season after the team traded away longtime franchise staples LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges.

The Hornets selected Miller with the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

articles.headline: LaFleur enthused Packers RB Jacobs, 'an elite-level back,' might play Sunday
articles.description: Green Bay's Josh Jacobs, ''an elite-level back'' in the eyes of Packers coach Matt LaFleur, will return to practice Wednesday and has a chance to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions after missing six games while on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.
articles.headlineJa: ラフル、パッカーズのRBジェイコブスを「エリート級」と絶賛、日曜の試合に出場か
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズのマット・ラフル監督が「エリート級のバック」と称するグリーンベイのジョシュ・ジェイコブスは、NFLのコミッショナー免除リストにより6試合を欠場していたが、水曜日に練習に復帰し、日曜日のデトロイト・ライオンズ戦に出場する可能性がある。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will return to practice Wednesday and has a chance to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions after missing the first six games of the season while on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.

However, the return of pass rusher Micah Parsons will have to wait. Coach Matt LaFleur said Parsons will not return to practice this week, and with a Thursday game the following week, it might be a couple more weeks before he hits the field for the first time since last year's ACL surgery.

Jacobs has been able to do just about everything except practice or play in games while on the exempt list.

"We feel like he's in a pretty good spot," LaFleur said Monday. "He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football."

"He could go to meetings, he could lift with our strength coaches and condition with them," LaFleur added. "He couldn't go to any of the team activities -- the practices and whatnot. He's been engaged and he's been working out."

Without Jacobs, who is still being investigated by the NFL for personal conduct policy violations stemming from his misdemeanor battery charge earlier this year, the Packers have by far the worst rushing offense in the NFL through six games. Their 59.8 yards rushing per game is last in the NFL by more than 16 yards, and that average is the third lowest by any team through six games in the past 20 years. The Packers have failed to reach 100 yards rushing as a team in any game this season but have still managed to win four of six games.

"Well, I think he's an elite-level back," LaFleur said. "He's certainly not going to hurt it. I think he can provide a spark."

LaFleur said that the team will determine Jacobs' status for Sunday against the Lions later in the week but that if all goes well during practice, he thinks Jacobs will make an immediate impact.

"That's going to be determined throughout the course of the week, see where he's at, see how he's feeling, and then we'll make a decision," LaFleur said.

Jacobs still could miss additional games pending the outcome of the NFL's investigation, which is ongoing. If he is suspended for only six games, then the time on the commissioner exempt list would cover the suspension. If he's suspended for any more than six games, then he would miss additional games. It's possible he could return to play but have to miss games at a later date.

Jacobs was placed on the commissioner exempt list Aug. 30 while the NFL continued to gather information about the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay.

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property. articles.headline: Lakers waive former first-round pick Dalton Knecht
articles.description: The Los Angeles Lakers waived their 2024 first-round pick Dalton Knecht on Monday, the team announced.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers waived their 2024 first-round pick Dalton Knecht on Monday, the team announced.

The Lakers had 16 players under contract and needed to cut down to 15 -- the most an NBA roster can carry -- by Monday's 5 p.m. ET deadline.

Knecht was selected with the No. 17 pick in 2024 after a standout junior season at the University of Tennessee. The 6-foot-6 wing enjoyed a hot start to his pro career -- including one nine-game stretch from mid- to late November his rookie season when he averaged 18.9 points on 55.4% shooting (52.2% from 3), 4.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists -- but struggled to replicate that success since.

In February 2025, the Lakers traded Knecht, Cam Reddish, a 2031 unprotected first-round pick and a 2030 pick swap to the Charlotte Hornets for center Mark Williams, but the trade was rescinded after Williams failed the physical exam.

Knecht finished his rookie season averaging 9.1 points on 46.1% shooting (37.6% from 3) and 2.8 rebounds in 19.2 minutes across 78 games. In his second year, his playing time was cut to 10.2 minutes in 54 games and he averaged 4.2 points on 45.5% shooting (34.2% from 3) and 1.4 rebounds.

In four preseason appearances this month, Knecht averaged 2.8 points on 25% shooting (14.3% from 3) and 1.3 rebounds in 11.9 minutes per game.

The Lakers pursued 2-for-1 trade opportunities to move Knecht and another player to acquire an additional big man, league sources told ESPN, but could not find a deal by Monday's deadline.

Prior to L.A.'s preseason finale against the Denver Nuggets last week, Lakers coach JJ Redick was asked what he thought stalled Knecht's momentum with the franchise.

"I think the biggest thing is the team changed," Redick said. "The team changed. The needs changed, the fit changed. I think he got better as a player over the last two years. I think each guy has, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the amount of injuries we had. So, I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he's in a tough spot right now."

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: How Davante Adams injury affects Rams
articles.description: What should fantasy managers do with Davante Adams set to miss the next 6-10 weeks?
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 19: How Davante Adams injury affects Rams offense

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The news on Davante Adams' injury suffered Sunday is devastating, as Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that the veteran wide receiver has a ruptured hamstring and will miss 6 to 10 weeks. Adams is the No. 7 wide receiver in fantasy points (102.0, or 17.0 per game), and he had been a top-10 weekly scorer in three of his first five games.

A 6-to-10 week timetable effectively ends Adams' fantasy regular season, as the midpoint of that range would take us through Week 14, directly before standard league playoffs begin. Though most leagues offer IR spots in which he could be stashed, steering through the bye weeks while keeping him there -- even if you're granted two or more of them -- isn't easy to do. If you need roster flexibility for bye weeks or injury fill-ins, it's reasonable to drop Adams in order to seek replacements. For now, try to keep him stashed there once he's officially moved to injured reserve, considering his past production and fantasy playoffs utility. The Rams have an extremely favorable Week 15 matchup for the position (DAL), as one example.

In Adams' absence, the Rams' offense takes a noticeable hit, as Adams and fellow Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had accounted for 42% of the team's total targets for the season, and that's despite Nacua having missed two games due to a groin injury. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington will all likely see expanded roles while Adams is out, with Mumpfied the closest to fantasy relevant and more so in 12-team leagues with deep benches or 14-plus-team formats. Be aware, however, that those three totaled 12 targets and 24.4 fantasy points during Nacua's Weeks 2-3 absences, reflecting their low priority in the receiving pecking order.

It's the Rams' tight ends who should benefit most while Adams heals, as was the case in those same Weeks 2-3 games. Terrance Ferguson scored 17.4 fantasy points on nine targets in Week 2, before injuring his MCL in Week 3 and landing on IR. Tyler Higbee emerged with 20.2 fantasy points on 11 targets in Week 3, and he has now averaged 12.4 points and 6.8 targets in the past four weeks. Higbee is a definite add in any league larger than ESPN's standard, and Ferguson, who is eligible to return in Week 8, could warrant similar appeal if he's ready to play a week from now.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the most important offseason signings, including Cason Wallace's $139 million extension with the Thunder.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason still features plenty of important moves across the league.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Oct. 18: Thunder, Wallace agree to long-term extension

Cason Wallace terms: Five years, $139 million

Grade: B-

Wallace's contract, worth $27.8 million per year, is right in line with the going rate for young, defense-first perimeter players. Other recent rookie extensions include $31 million per year for Ausar Thompson, $30 million per year for Jalen Suggs and $25 million per year for Dyson Daniels.

Granted, the extensions for Suggs and Daniels haven't aged especially well since they were signed, given both players' offensive regressions.

There's good reason for the Thunder to believe Wallace is worth this contract, however, in a vacuum: A second-team All-Defensive honoree last season with one of the highest annual steal rates, he's one of the NBA's best perimeter stoppers, and he seems to have yet-untapped offensive potential, as well. He has never averaged more than 8.6 points in a season, but he's a career 37% 3-point shooter. And over a 15-game stretch last winter, mostly with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sidelined, Wallace averaged 13.9 points and 4.7 assists while assuming much greater offensive responsibilities.

The Thunder are betting there's more where that burst came from, now that Wallace is presumably set to take Luguentz Dort's spot in the starting lineup. He can defend most of the same stars Dort used to guard, while adding more offensive oomph and playmaking against elite defenses. In the conference finals against San Antonio, for example, Dort averaged 4.3 points and made 20% of his 3s, while Wallace averaged 10.1 points and made 50% of his 3s.

But this extension doesn't come in a vacuum; rather, it comes amid a threatening financial backdrop for Oklahoma City, which already had to trade Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this summer for financial reasons. And the purse strings could get even tighter next year, when Gilgeous-Alexander's supermax extension kicks in.

To that end, one of the most important executive quotes of this summer came from the Thunder's Sam Presti, who told Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman, "The impression I have been given is that the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be reallocated to future teams."

Those savings will need to be reallocated for Wallace's extension

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Hoop Collection: The biggest questions in the NBA's Atlantic Division

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to welcome in ESPN analyst and radio host Tim Hahn for a preview of the NBA's Atlantic Division. The trio covers how the New York Knicks will defend their title, what changes to expect with the Philadelphia 76ers and if the Boston Celtics big moves will pay off. They close on how high Kawhi Leonard can lift the Toronto Raptors this season and some injury updates.

Hahn on how to keep Karl-Anthony Towns happy this season: "I can tell you from talking to him, on the side conversations, not in interviews, but [him] almost pleading because, people would ask him about shots. 'You only took four shots in the first half. What happened?' And all that stuff.

"And it was one time I was walking away and he kind of grabbed me. He's like, 'It's not about shots. I don't care about shots.' He said, 'I just [like] being involved.' He's like, 'I love to pass the ball. I just I want to help my teammates.'  And so when they when they moved more in that Atlanta series, which turned everything into him being a hub of the offense, he was the happiest. I'm telling you this is not propaganda, he really was. He was happy because he loves to pass. And if you see the flare with the different ways he passes the basketball and the smile on his face, he wears 32, his father's number, but it's also Magic Johnson. And he has told that story many times. He loves that.

"So what Windy's saying, that's literally the truth. If you want to keep him happy, keep him involved and everything else will figure itself out."

articles.headline: Dejan Kulusevski makes Tottenham return 526 days after suffering knee injury
articles.description: Dejan Kulusevski played his first match for 526 days on Monday after he came off the bench in the 86th minute of Tottenham's Premier League match against Coventry on Monday.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Dejan Kulusevski played his first match for 526 days on Monday after he came off the bench in the 86th minute of Tottenham's Premier League 3-1 victory over Coventry City on Monday.

Kulusevski, 26, suffered a serious knee injury in what appeared to be a seemingly innocuous 19th-minute collision with Marc Guéhi when Spurs played Crystal Palace on the final day of the 2024-25 season.

Then-Spurs manager Ange Postecoglou said the following day that Kulusevski's injury "looks like a knock," but it turned out to be a complex knee injury that has required surgery and seen the player suffer multiple setbacks.

Kulusevski celebrated Spurs' Europa League final triumph over Manchester United while on crutches later that month.

He has said he underwent "knee patella [kneecap] cartilage surgery" to treat the complex injury which saw him miss out on Sweden's World Cup squad.

Tottenham have fired three managers while the Swede has been sidelined -- Postecoglou, Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor -- as the team recorded consecutive 17th-place finishes in the Premier League.

Kulusevski, who shared that he underwent a knee arthroscopy in March which he said "took out what was not supposed to be there" returned to full Spurs training on Aug. 31 before suffering another minor setback in September.

He is one of several Spurs players to have suffered serious injuries over the past year, with an unusually high percentage of them affecting the knee.

But his return has come at a good time for Roberto De Zerbi who revealed that Sávio and Lucas Bergvall have been added to the club's lengthy list of absentees for the coming weeks.

Before suffering the injury, Kulusevski had developed into one of Spurs' most important players following his move from Juventus on an initial loan deal in 2022.
